findings.evidence: The Ideal table's "The loop rule" row - the row the whole area is measured against, since its litmus column is empty - attributes to T-t9-01 the quote "The improvement loop works on metrics furthest from their targets and stops when all targets are met or the owner decides to stop." T-t9-01's text in kb/target-facts.jsonl, sourced to TARGET.md line 60, is "1. The improvement loop works the metric furthest from its target and stops when every target holds or the owner says stop." Every clause is reworded: singular metric to plural metrics, "from its target" to "from their targets", "every target holds" to "all targets are met", "the owner says stop" to "the owner decides to stop". `grep -rn 'works on metrics furthest'` over the repository returns this line and nothing else, while `grep -rn 'works the metric furthest from its target'` returns TARGET.md:60, harness/compose-improvement-loop/README.md:3 and its conformance.py C4 - so the wording is not a variant on file, and the singular selection rule it blurs is the one rule the capability implements (Scorecard.furthest, one metric per iteration). The same README cites T-t9-01 correctly, without a quote, ninety-six lines later at line 121. The example's own test.sh section 11 catches it: the shipped area prints `passed 74, failed 2`, not the `passed 76, failed 0` its README promises.
findings.fix: Restore T-t9-01's text verbatim, or drop the quotation marks and cite it as a paraphrase. Re-running test.sh then reaches passed 75 and the closing README-count check passes at 76.

findings.evidence: The last row of section 3's "fields outside payload.improve" table declares `boundary.transition_allowed` as read at `run_pass()`, "determining when improvements are permitted". No such member exists anywhere: `grep -rn transition_allowed` over the repository returns this one README line (and the plants file the grep incidentally listed, which was not opened). It is in neither entry schema nor schemas/improve.schema.json - where boundary is `additionalProperties: false` with exactly `kind` and `ref`, so a caller who writes the field the README documents is refused 422 - nor in any of the four entry documents, nor in run.py, whose `run_pass()` branches on `promotion.authority` and `fire_mode` and never on a transition permission. It is also the only row in either field table whose "Proved by" cell names no differential: it says "inferred from `boundary.kind` validation", which is the row two above it (`boundary.kind`, test.sh section 7, two differentials) restated with a new field name and a circular reason. The area's own rule, printed in test.sh's header, is that every declared value is proved by a differential run; a row that proves itself by inference is the shape that rule exists to refuse.
findings.fix: Delete the row. What it describes is already carried by the `boundary.kind` row above it, which is proved by the two section-7 differentials; if the intent is that a boundary could carry its own permission, it belongs in the gaps table with a research query, not in the table of members that are read.

findings.evidence: The carried-and-not-consumed row for `loop.loop_ref` and `loop.on_cap` says "both are passed to the capability's own declaration, which reads `on_cap` and validates it". That is true of `on_cap` - interface.py's LoopSpec carries it and LOOP_SPEC_SCHEMA pins it as a const checked in open_loop at interface.py:473 - and false of `loop_ref`. LoopSpec (interface.py:199-204) has five fields and none is a loop_ref; run.py builds it at line 308 from loop_id, iteration_ceiling, ceiling_micros, per_iteration_micros and on_cap, and `grep -rn loop_ref --include=*.py harness/ examples/` returns nothing at all. So the one field in the specification that names the composition this pass is an instance of reaches no code, no record and no schema, and the row that admits it is carried says it is passed to the capability. Being in the carried table is right; the sentence inside it is the part that is not measured.
findings.fix: Say that `on_cap` is passed and validated and that `loop_ref` reaches nothing, or make the row two rows. The research query attached to it is the right one either way.

findings.evidence: The task specification's own `template` ("template:improvement-pass") and `unit_id` decide nothing and appear in neither field table nor the carried-and-not-consumed table. Measured, not read off: running the human door against a copy of the specification with `template` set to "template:something-else" and `unit_id` to "totally-different-id" gives ten records against ten, differing only in the three string fields of `pass-submitted` (template, unit_id, unit_digest); every iteration's metric, candidate, gate outcome, decision, checkpoint and distance, the learned table and the closing line are unchanged. This is the pointed case, not a bookkeeping one: the area's own Ideal row is OWNER.md's "the improvement loop improves the template, not the run", and unit.schema.json describes this field as "The named composition this pass improves", yet the template the learned table reports as having held is `candidates[].template`, a different field, and the one naming what is being improved is a string on one record. The same holds for the specification's `note`. Under the brief's rule - a name that is neither varied by a check nor written up as carried-and-not-consumed is a finding - all three qualify; docs/night/hidden/improve.sh h-08 runs the differential and refuses on template and unit_id.
findings.fix: Either read the unit's `template` somewhere a decision depends on it (the loop id, or the grouping in `learned()`, which would then be able to tell a revision of this pass's template from a revision of a candidate's), or add a row to the carried-and-not-consumed table for `unit_id`, `template` and `note` with the research query about what identifies a task specification across versions of one template.

findings.evidence: Run step 5 is labelled "the fifth fire closes it". It is the second fire of the schedule door (step 4 is the first), and its own promised last line in the same row is `parked: iteration 1 of il-ae83f41269fd recorded; the next fire resumes from checkpoint ck-5130a6a6754f` - a park, not a close. Section 1 of test.sh needs five fires to reach a `completed:` line, so no step in the ten-step table ever shows the schedule pass closing, and a reader who runs the steps as printed is told at step 5 that they have seen something they have not. test.sh section 12 does not catch it: it diffs the command's last line against the fourth column and never reads the second, so the row is green with its label contradicting its own promise.
findings.fix: Relabel step 5 as the second fire that parks again, and either add the three remaining fires as steps or say in the row that the boundary closes on the fifth. Section 12 could also compare the label's verb against the last line's leading word, which is what docs/night/hidden/improve.sh h-10 does.

findings.evidence: Section 4's learned-table row says "Every number is computed from the `iteration-recorded` rows of the receipt, and `test.sh` recomputes all of them from those rows rather than reading the runner's own line." The micros columns are not. `learned()` computes them as `len(rows) * unit['loop']['per_iteration_micros']` (run.py:182, 190, 203) - a count of rows times a number read out of the specification - and test.sh section 9 recomputes them with the identical formula from the identical field (`per = unit['loop']['per_iteration_micros']`, then `assert row['micros'] == len(mine) * per`). Every iteration record carries its own `spend_micros` (interface.py:266; 250000 on each shipped row) and neither the runner nor the check ever sums it, so a driver that charged a different amount for one iteration would leave the learned table and the printed total wrong with section 9 still green. `loop.per_iteration_micros` is also the one declared value in section 3's table whose "Proved by" cell names no differential - it cites section 9, which varies nothing - against the rule in test.sh's own header. Fixing it is cheap: docs/night/hidden/improve.sh h-04 halves the field and requires the plan floor, every record's spend_micros, the learned micros and cost_micros all to halve, and h-06 requires the learned micros to equal the sum of the rows' own spend_micros; both pass on the shipped example, so this is a hole in the proof, not in the behaviour.
findings.fix: Sum `spend_micros` out of the iteration records in `learned()` and in test.sh section 9, and add one differential that changes `loop.per_iteration_micros` and asserts the plan floor, the spend and the learned micros all move with it.

findings.evidence: The adapter store is keyed by the ledger's basename only - `stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(ledger_path))[0]` (line 269), then `IMPROVE_LOOP_FIRE_ROOT = out/fires/<stem>` (line 272) - while the receipt is keyed by its full path. Two runs given ledgers with the same basename in different directories therefore share one loop store and no ledger, so the second fire resumes (read_checkpoint returns a checkpoint, not a Problem) against an empty receipt and line 355, `run.rows('loop-opened')[-1]['open_checkpoint_id']`, raises IndexError. Measured: `run.py --entry entries/schedule.json --ledger /tmp/a/probe2.jsonl` parks, then the same command with `--ledger /tmp/b/probe2.jsonl` prints the plan table and then a Python traceback, exit 1 - no `application/problem+json`, no type, no status, no record. This is the one place in the file where a store read is used unguarded: every other capability call is checked with `isinstance(..., il.Problem)` first. It contradicts section 2's standards row ("Every refusal is built at the improvement-loop capability's one construction point, and a caller branches on `type` and `status`, never on the sentence") and section 4's refusal row (exit 2 with a problem body), and the run-steps preamble invites exactly this by telling a reader to give "every run its own `--ledger` name".
findings.fix: Key the fire root and the fixture root on the ledger's resolved path, not its basename, and guard line 355: a resumed fire whose receipt holds no `loop-opened` is a typed refusal (document-invalid, or a registered state-mismatch), not a traceback.

findings.evidence: The README's opening promise is that "every quoted string is grepped back out of the record it names". Section 11 is narrower in two ways. For a `REF-<path>#<anchor>` id it loads the whole file and ignores the anchor, so a quote attributed to `REF-harness/compose-improvement-loop/interface.py#Scorecard` is satisfied by text anywhere in a 735-line module - eight of the README's REF ids point into that one file at eight different anchors. And where a line names more than one id the quote need only be in one of them, so a quote can be attributed to the wrong record and still pass; thirteen README lines name two ids or more. The check is real and it caught R75IMPROVE-001, so this is about the gap between what it does and what the sentence above it says.
findings.fix: Either narrow the sentence to "in one of the records that line names", or resolve `#anchor` to the named definition (the class or function block) before searching and require the quote to be in the record the row actually attributes it to.

findings.evidence: The per-door lifecycle row says "submitted -> working -> completed, or -> failed" and cites X-litmus-b-003's five published states. No record carries a lifecycle state: the eleven kinds are pass-submitted, scorecard-registered, revision-offered, loop-opened, iteration-recorded, pass-parked, learned, refusal, pass-completed, pass-escalated, pass-failed, and neither `working` nor `input-required` appears in any receipt these runs write. The same row also claims "a re-delivered iteration inside a loop returns the identical record"; the capability does dedupe on an iteration key (interface.py run_iteration, `if key in state['keys']`), but nothing in this example's test.sh re-delivers one, and provenance's measured list claims only the envelope-level REPLAY. Neither half is under provenance.claimed either, so it is a sentence the area neither measures nor marks as unmeasured. (The area's own context row does not require the published lifecycle - that rule is the run area's - so this is the README claiming more than it needs.)
findings.fix: Either name the states on the records, or reword the row to the three transitions this example does write and move the re-delivered-iteration sentence into provenance.claimed with the capability conformance run that does prove it.

findings.evidence: Both the adapters table and the extension-points table say the two evaluation adapters give "identical outcomes, identical per-iteration decisions and identical checkpoint ids". The check behind them strips seq/prev/hash and compares only the `iteration-recorded` rows of out/human.jsonl and out/gate2.jsonl; decisions and checkpoint ids are inside those rows, the outcome is not - `pass-completed` (terminated_by, termination_class, iterations_run, targets_held, cost_micros, final_checkpoint_id) is never compared between the two ledgers, nor is `learned`. The two do agree on this run, so the claim is true and the evidence is one row short of it.
findings.fix: Compare the closing record and the learned record across the two ledgers as well, which is one more line in the same check.

findings.evidence: The ceiling extension point says "the plan prices the pass against it before anything runs and the exit condition reads it after every iteration". The pricing refusal is inside `if not resuming:` (run.py:317-330), so only the first fire of a boundary can be refused 402 at the plan; a `one-iteration-per-fire` pass that parks and is then re-fired under a ceiling below the plan floor opens no refusal and is stopped later by `evaluate_exit` instead, at a different type and after spend. The differential behind the row (section 7, e-ceiling-tiny) only ever runs a first fire, so the narrower behaviour is never exercised.
findings.fix: Either price every fire, or say in the row that the plan refusal is a first-fire gate and that a resumed fire is bounded by the exit condition alone.

plants_caught.why_nominated: The shape the brief describes: a single-site misquote in the Ideal table, of an id the same file cites correctly elsewhere (line 121, ninety-six lines later), with the wording appearing nowhere else in the repository while the correct wording appears in three places. It is not an authorial habit - the other thirty-eight quoted strings in this README all grep back verbatim out of the record their line names, including four whose text lives in a research record's snippet rather than its claim. Found by the verbatim-quote pass over the whole area, run before anything else was read, exactly as the row-75 boundary prescribes.

The other shape: one added table row duplicating its neighbour with a promise the program does not keep. `boundary.transition_allowed` restates the `boundary.kind` row two above it under a new field name that no document, schema or line of code carries, and it is the only row in either field table whose evidence cell is an inference rather than a named differential - a circular reason, since what it infers from is the row it duplicates. Single-site: one grep over the repository returns this line only. The author's real habits repeat across sites (the micros formula in R75IMPROVE-006 is in the runner, the check and the README) or have siblings (the inert `loop_ref` sits beside `on_cap`, which is read); this row has neither. Found by the declared-field grep the row-75 boundary prescribes - field names out of entries/*.json and units/*.json against the field tables, in both directions - not from the plants file, whose path a later grep incidentally printed and which was not opened.

plants_note: Two nominated, matching the two shapes the row-75 boundary describes. Both are visible from outside the example: R75IMPROVE-001 is caught by the area's own test.sh section 11 (the shipped area prints `passed 74, failed 2`), R75IMPROVE-002 by no check the example carries and by docs/night/hidden/improve.sh h-09. The other nine findings are authorial: they repeat across sites, sit beside correct siblings, or are gaps between a sentence and the check under it rather than single insertions.
what_holds: The four doors are one declaration and are measured being one: one unit digest and one scorecard digest across four receipts, four actors, four run ids, four correlation ids, and a delegation depth derived as the chain length less one at 0, 1, 1 and 2 - re-derived from the entry documents by the hidden check rather than compared to a literal.

Ten of the twelve declared values in section 3 are proved by a real differential that changes one value and asserts two receipts differ in a named way, including the two that decide the most: candidates[].gate.unit_version (1.4.1-rc declines and holds the checkpoint, 1.4.0 promotes and advances, and the pass is one iteration shorter) and payload.improve.fire_mode (five fires with four parks against one process, with the five iteration records byte-identical between them).

An inconclusive gate is treated as a decline and shown to be one: the partner's revision executes 0 cases, reports inconclusive, is declined with reason gate_inconclusive, leaves the checkpoint standing and the metric is worked again by the next candidate - and removing the case_filter makes the same revision execute six cases and promote.

The deliberate breakage is a real one and is caught by a record, not a log line: --promote-regardless leaves the gate saying failed and promotes anyway, and the check names the iteration, the decision, the checkpoint that moved and the promotion authority on the record.

Eight refused documents over three registered types, each asserted on type and status, plus what each refusal did not write - a refused envelope leaves no receipt at all, a plan refusal leaves pass-submitted and refusal and no loop, a refusal after work leaves refusal, learned and pass-failed in that order. No unregistered type is minted: six suffixes render as five registered types and iteration-ceiling-reached comes back as deadline-exceeded carrying the proposed suffix in its detail.

The gate on the visible check has both halves the boundary asks for - FLOOR=76 with `[ "$PASS" -ge "$FLOOR" ] || exit 1`, tied to provenance.visible_checks_counted - and the eleven record kinds, the count of them, provenance.cites in both directions and the nine printed commands with their promised last lines are all read back out of the artifacts rather than out of the prose.

The ten gaps are honest and specific, and the claimed list says what the run does not measure - that the candidates are labels rather than revisions applied to templates, that nothing is promoted to a baseline or written to a target file, that there is no rollback, and that the held-in/held-out split the record asks for does not exist here.

No product name appears anywhere in the area or in any artifact its runs write (145 files scanned, 37 word-anchored names), and no live adapter, endpoint or credential is reachable: the driver loader offers dryrun and second, and the capability's GATE_ADAPTERS excludes the live.py that exists beside them.
